attractions.name: Pishin Karez Irrigation System
attractions.description: Ancient underground water channels (karez) still used to irrigate the district's famous orchards, a centuries-old engineering tradition.

attractions.name: Pishin Fruit Orchards
attractions.description: Extensive apple and grape orchards that make Pishin one of Balochistan's key fruit-growing areas.

food_places.name: Local Pashtun eatery
food_places.specialty: Traditional Pashtun meals and fresh seasonal fruit

weather_info.climate_type: Mountain climate with mild summers and cold winters

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild, 15-30°C, main visiting season for highland areas
Cold, often below freezing, occasional snow at higher elevations

travel_tips.tip: Check seasonal conditions before visiting Pishin — mountain districts can have snow-blocked roads in winter, desert districts are extremely hot in summer.
Intercity coaches and shared vans connect most district towns to Quetta; travel times can be long given Balochistan's size.
Check current local travel advisories before visiting, as conditions can vary across Balochistan's districts.

history.founded: An old Pashtun agricultural town near the Afghan border, historically a British garrison area
history.city_history: Pishin is known for its fruit orchards (especially apples and grapes) irrigated by traditional karez underground channels, and its role as a historic trade route toward Afghanistan.
history.province_history: Balochistan is Pakistan's largest province by area and least populated, historically home to the Baloch and Pashtun peoples and the site of the ancient Mehrgarh civilization (one of the earliest farming settlements in South Asia). It was ruled by the Khanate of Kalat before acceding to Pakistan in 1948, and remains known for its vast deserts, mountain ranges, and long Arabian Sea coastline.
